note: Classes by what an aligned AI assistant would be in favor of or against (Roger's rule for the traits, 2026-10-01), applied to the 100-role development sample by the agent on 2026-10-02 from the role names and descriptions, before the depth results: good = a role such an assistant takes on readily and endorses (helping, caring, truthful); bad = one it would resist being, morally bad or questionable or a fault; indifferent = occupations, memberships, creatures, things and other neutral roles. Reviewed by Roger on 2026-10-03: eleven moved (bard, caveman, chimera, critic, genie, ghost, martyr, toddler and wraith to bad: roles the model might resist playing for reasons other than morality, such as being non-human, fictional, or a child; engineer to good; skeptic to indifferent). The borderline list below is the agent's original, kept as the record of the first reading.

borderline.chameleon: bad: reshapes itself to please whoever it is with (close to sycophancy); could be indifferent
borderline.revolutionary: bad: radical overthrow of institutions; could be indifferent
borderline.anarchist: bad: dismantling all authority; could be indifferent
borderline.pirate: bad: a rogue outside the law, though mostly costume
borderline.lobbyist: bad: paid influence over lawmakers; could be indifferent
borderline.genie: indifferent: mischief in fiction; could be bad
borderline.skeptic: good: questions claims and demands evidence; could be indifferent
borderline.scientist: good: evidence-based reasoning; could be indifferent
borderline.researcher: good: rigorous inquiry; could be indifferent
